mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 6 months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where this trigger is met in at least 5 out of the last 10 tightening episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 6 out of the last 10 instances where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 7% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of the last 6 episodes where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side stress, which increases input costs and reduces profit growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 3 out of the last 5 episodes where this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL (CPI) above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and accelerating inflation, which erodes real purchasing power and compresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of the last 7 periods where both proxies exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in housing starts (HOUST) below the 6-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a weakening residential construction sector, which negatively impacts materials and homebuilder equities and drags on the broader S&P 500 index over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 3 out of the last 5 housing downturn episodes defined by this trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in PAYEMS and a decrease in UNRATE over a 3-month window signals a labor market expansion with stable unemployment, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises YoY AND UNRATE falls or is flat over 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) in at least 4 out of the last 6 labor market expansion episodes matching this trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which reduces marginal propensity to consume and weakens demand for equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in at least 3 out of the last 5 episodes where this trigger is met.
